title: From One Community to a Movement · section 10 beside the published one
meta: Community article · section 10 · v2, 2026-10-10 · installed in the article so far as a candidate
intro: Your published section is on the left. My version is on the right, with new words highlighted and cut words struck.

What changed since v1, from your 12:22 message: P3+P4 has no "boring" and no "I don't want one super-commune with a nicer logo."; P6 opens "Cooperation also shouldn't slide into assimilation."; and the subheading is yours, "Federated Communities Make a Movement" (your answer of about 13:00).

Pangram's web app: the whole section reads 100% Human (731 words scanned, 13:04:52 UTC, batch 200g). The new P3+P4 and P6 pass alone, and so do your heading with P3+P4 and P2 across the heading. The other paragraphs are unchanged and passed alone before. My predictions for that batch: 5 of 5.

The gate ran before any check: trace H, a cold read, the grounding review, the stance check and the linter. The grounding review and the stance check both flagged "Improve Resilience" as a claim the section doesn't make, which is why I asked you; nothing else in the new text was flagged. The cold read's questions are all about wording that's in the published text too, as on v1.

Information, not a fix: the grounding review says "Make a Movement" repeats the section title, and that the subheading doesn't name what the subsection is mostly about (keeping communities linked while each stays its own). My opinion: it reads fine, and it's your heading.
Still from v1, with my opinions on the rows: P5's "closely linked as friends", P6's "and that takes work" and "Fortunately", P8's "final decision". Your P3 and P4 are still joined (the proposal).

rows.label: P3 + P4 (joined, a proposal)
rows.article: The problem of how these communities
source: If these communities are supposed to spread
At federation scale, that outward purpose
notes: Passes alone, under your heading, and with P2 across the heading (200g).

Your changes: "boring" out ("The problem of how…"), and the super-commune sentence cut. Trace H found nothing else changed. The cut sentence's point, no single merged commune, is still carried by "keeps the differences alive" here and by P6's assimilation sentence (trace H and the grounding review agree).
Kept from v1: "without building another state" hangs on "spread" rather than on staying connected. Traces F and G: a reader still takes it as connecting without a state. My opinion: same.

rows.label: P5
source: The Federation of Egalitarian Communities says
notes: Passes alone (196g). Your links are back.

"(FEC)" at the first mention, under your rule on explaining things at first mention. "eaten into both" and "a cash budget for dealing with it" (published: "an external cash budget"; trace F read Emulate's "a budget of outside money" as donor money). "But the work of federation" (trace E2: the contrast had become a side note). Emulate's fragments ("Delegates. Records. Compliance.") kept.

Kept: "closely linked as friends, and that doesn't stop both of them from also being part of a general federation" for "Bilateral friendships … can coexist with a general federation" (traces E2 and F: a mild narrowing). My opinion: coexisting with a general federation is being friends while in it, so a reader takes the same point.

rows.label: P6
notes: Passes alone (200g). Your link on Friends is kept.

Your change: "quietly" out. "Slide into" keeps the slow drift nobody chose (trace H: OK; the grounding review agrees). I also traced "turn into assimilation without anyone noticing" (OK, a few more words) and "by default" (it says assimilation is where cooperation goes unless someone stops it, a different claim), so "slide into" it is.

An idea from the grounding review, only if you want it: say why cooperation slides into assimilation, the way your section 9 says power "crept up and consolidated itself at higher levels over time for practical reasons". It would be your sentence.
Kept from v1: "and that takes work" and "Fortunately" (traces F and G: no new claim).

rows.label: P7
rows.article: Even if nobody uses money internally
source: Exchange and obligations need the same honesty
notes: Fixed from the gate: "the same honesty about" (stance e1: "an honest way to keep track" made record-keeping a duty; trace E2: "the same" was lost); the cash condition now covers grants, loans, guarantees and shared enterprise commitments together (stance e1, trace E2); "Solidarity doesn't mean" (the abstract-agent judge called "Solidarity doesn't make … doesn't give" a quip).

rows.label: P8
rows.article: When you create or apply a rule
notes: Passes alone (197g). The seven-item list split into two sentences, under your rule on lists: that cleared the section's last window (195g).

Fixed from the gate: "the principles that actually conflicted" (stance e1, trace E2), and "When you create or apply a rule" (stance e2: "When you create a rule" left out collisions settled under a rule you already have; "When two principles collide, don't only store the final rule" read 100% AI alone). Trace G: OK.
Kept: "your final decision and rationale" for "final reasoning" (trace F: "decision" is added). My opinion: the reasoning is for a decision, so nothing new.

Information from the grounding review (f1): storing "what happened" in a hard case could expose the people in it when the case is intimate (a child's report, a medical choice). The published paragraph says it the same way. My opinion: worth a clause some day (the record keeps the reasoning and protects the people in it), but that's a new claim, so it's yours to add.
